userStories.title: Listing Quality Score: one 0–100 number per listing aggregating every verified ranking lever
userStories.description: As a seller, I want a single score telling me how well each listing plays eBay's actual ranking game — and exactly which fix earns the most points — so optimizing 300 drafts stops requiring SEO knowledge. Audit: no listing-quality score exists anywhere (verified against current prd + archive); components exist piecemeal (aspect blockers, compliance card, category nudge).
acceptanceCriteria: Edge lib computes score + component breakdown from verified levers only: title quality (US-1890 lint + utilization), required+recommended aspect coverage (US-1895 math), photo standards (US-1896 data: count, hero type, dimensions), category confidence (leaf + suggestion match), condition-tier/description consistency (US-1894), and fulfillment signals read from the listing's resolved business policies (returns accepted, ≤1-day handling, free-shipping) — weights documented in the lib with playbook citations

Returned in the validate/preflight response and persisted on the listing row for sorting; drafts list + pipeline board show the score with a breakdown popover where each component links to its fix surface
Score never invents folklore signals (no Best Offer, no relist-freshness); copy for fulfillment components cites 'eBay Best Match factors'
Deno tests: component fixtures produce expected scores; a fully-optimized fixture scores 100

iOS surfaces the same score: PublishDialog shows the score + component breakdown (each component naming its fix surface) read from the validate/preflight response the app already calls, and drafts-library rows show a score chip usable for sorting — no client-side recomputation of weights (parity audit 2026-07-09: original criteria covered only the web drafts list + pipeline board)
userStories.notes: [P2][SEO][Capstone] Depends on US-1890/1894/1895/1896 landing first (build after them). See EBAY_RANKING_PLAYBOOK.md. Added 2026-07-09. | PARTIAL 2026-07-18 (agent loop — story stays passes:false). Dependencies confirmed landed first (US-1890/1894/1895/1896 + US-1490 all archived passes:true), so the capstone is genuinely unblocked. DONE: AC1 scoring lib + AC3 + AC4. New lib/listing-quality-score.ts — pure, every input supplied by the caller because assemblePublishContext already computes all six signals in one pass. Weights sum to 100 and each cites its EBAY_RANKING_PLAYBOOK.md section: aspects 30 (§1 'single highest-confidence lever'), photos 25 (§6 thumbnail = 'biggest CTR lever'), title 15, category 12, fulfillment 10 (§4 eBay-CONFIRMED returns/≤1-day handling/free shipping), condition 8. The playbook publishes NO numbers deliberately, so the values are a judgement call but the ORDERING is not — a test pins aspects > photos > title > fulfillment. New lib/business-policy-signals.ts closes the gap the audit found: PolicySet carries only policy IDs, but syncBusinessPolicies already writes eBay's ENTIRE raw policy object into business_policies.policy_data, so the three fulfillment signals are parsed from that jsonb — nothing new is fetched. handlingTime is normalised across DAY/BUSINESS_DAY/HOUR (24h == 1 day, since rejecting it would under-score a seller who IS meeting the bar); free shipping accepts both the explicit flag and a zero shippingCost; a free INTERNATIONAL service does not count (Best Match ranks for the buyers being served). Everything fails to null, never false — 'unreadable policy' and 'seller refuses returns' are different facts and collapsing them would tell a seller to fix something already correct. AC3 (no folklore) drove a real design call. AC1's phrase 'title … utilization' invites rewarding titles near 80 chars — which is EXACTLY the vendor lore §2 flags as not an eBay statement. So title scores policy cleanliness (US-1890, a real blocker) plus a floor below which there is too little searchable text to match queries; there is no optimal band and no positional weighting. Tests assert 68 vs 78 chars TIE and that word order never moves the score, plus a guard that no component string mentions Best Offer / relist / Sell Similar / stemming / templates (§10 non-factors). TWO JUDGEMENT CALLS worth reviewing, both made after eyeballing the score across realistic listings rather than trusting green tests: (1) BLOCKED_SCORE_CEILING — the purely additive score LIED about exactly the listings a seller most needs to find: one missing required specific scored 70 and a non-leaf category scored 88, both for listings eBay refuses to list at all, so triaging 300 drafts by score would sort them into the 'fine' pile. Any publish-blocking component (no title, title policy violation, missing required aspect, no photos, sub-500px hero, non-leaf/not-found category) now caps the whole score at 40 and sets blocked + blockingReasons. A test asserts a blocked listing sorts BELOW the worst publishable one, and another asserts merely-weak listings are NOT marked blocked (a seller must be able to tell 'will not list' from 'will list badly'). (2) the aspects component was rebalanced from required 55%/recommended 45% to 25%/75% — paying most of the component for having no MISSING required aspect is paying for table stakes (it is a blocker otherwise), and it left recommended coverage barely moving the number (2/8 filled still scored 80; now 74). Unknown signals are excluded from BOTH numerator and denominator and the score rescales, so an unsynced business policy cannot drag a perfect listing below 100 — the score must not drift with OUR sync health. Verified: 25 tests in listing-quality-score_test.ts; full edge suite 4124 passed / 0 failed; deno lint (1168 files); deno check src/main.ts. NOT DONE (blocks passes): AC2 — the score is NOT yet returned from POST /listings/validate (the natural home is PublishContextOk in flipdesk-ebay.ts, which already computes every input) and NOT persisted on the listing row for sorting; persistence needs a migration + the drafts list / pipeline board breakdown popover. AC5 — iOS PublishDialog + drafts-library score chip; cannot be built or tested on Windows (Swift/xcodebuild is macOS-only). The lib is deliberately pure so both surfaces can consume it without recomputing weights client-side, which AC5 explicitly forbids. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AC2 FIRST HALF DONE: the score is now RETURNED from POST /listings/validate as qualityScore. assemblePublishContext gained a qualitySignals block carrying the RAW structured signals it already computes (title policy violations, photo blockers/warnings/count, category leaf status + whether it came from a Taxonomy suggestion, required-missing aspects) — deliberately raw, not a score, so the scorer never string-sniffs the blocker array, which would break silently the first time a message is reworded. The score itself is assembled in buildQualityScore() on the VALIDATE route, not inside assemblePublishContext, because it needs one extra DB read (business policies) and the publish + auto-publish paths share that function: scoring is a validate-time concern and the hot path should not pay for it. loadFulfillmentSignals() reads business_policies.policy_data tenant-scoped on user_id (US-268; ownerId comes from workspaceOwnerId ?? userId, never the body) and fails to UNKNOWN_FULFILLMENT so a policy read can never break a preflight. NOTABLE: this is the FIRST production caller of conditionDescriptionConsistency() — US-1894 (archived passes:true) shipped that check tested but never wired into any path, so the condition/description consistency it promised was not actually running anywhere until now. categoryWasSuggested maps to matchesSuggestion=true, and a hand-picked category stays null (unknown) rather than false: asserting false would penalise every category we never cross-checked. VERIFIED: the flipdesk-ebay.ts diff is 105 insertions and ZERO deletions — purely additive, no existing publish behaviour altered; deno check + deno lint (1168 files) clean; full edge suite 4124 passed / 0 failed. STILL OPEN for passes: AC2 second half — persisting the score on the listing row for sorting (needs a migration) + the drafts list / pipeline board breakdown popover; and AC5 iOS. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AC2 SECOND HALF — PERSISTENCE DONE. Migration 00476_listing_quality_score.sql adds listings.quality_score SMALLINT (0-100, NULL until first computed), quality_blocked BOOLEAN and quality_scored_at TIMESTAMPTZ, plus a 0-100 CHECK and a partial index (inventory_item_id, quality_score) WHERE quality_score IS NOT NULL for the drafts/pipeline sort. US-1108 triple satisfied: idempotent (ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS x3, duplicate_object-guarded ADD CONSTRAINT, CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS), EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped 00475->00476 in the SAME commit, self-record footer; schema-version_test.ts green. DESIGN CALLS: (1) the component BREAKDOWN is deliberately NOT stored — it is cheap to recompute (the preflight already loads every input), it changes whenever the weights change, and a stored copy would silently go stale and show a seller a breakdown that no longer matches the number beside it. Store the sortable scalar, recompute the explanation. (2) quality_score is NULLABLE with no default: NULL (never scored) and 0 (scored zero) are different states, and a NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 would make every unscored draft look broken and poison the sort. (3) quality_blocked is STORED rather than derived from score <= BLOCKED_SCORE_CEILING, because that ceiling is a policy constant that may move and old rows should stay honest if it does. WIRING: scoreAndPersist() on the validate route writes the scalar as a best-effort side effect — awaited but swallowed, because preflight is what tells a seller whether they can publish and must not start failing over a sort key (notably if the edge deploys ahead of 00476). A draft with no listings row yet is skipped: nothing to sort, nothing to store. Tenant-safe without an extra filter — ctx.listing came from assemblePublishContext, already owner-scoped, so the id is ours by construction and never from the request body (US-268). HELD MIGRATION: 00476 is committed locally and packaged in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md (apply AFTER 00475, then NOTIFY pgrst). No client-side read in this change, so the Pages auto-deploy is safe. Verified: deno check + lint (1168 files) + full edge suite 4126 passed / 0 failed. STILL OPEN for passes: AC2 UI (drafts list + pipeline board score chip and breakdown popover — the columns now exist to sort by) and AC5 iOS. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AC2 UI COMPONENT DONE — and my earlier claim that web UI was unverifiable here was WRONG. The repo has jsdom + 160 component tests that assert rendered markup via renderToStaticMarkup (no @testing-library) plus axe-core, so UI IS verifiable headless; I had assumed otherwise for several rounds without checking. New src/components/flipdesk/quality-score-chip.tsx exports QualityScoreChip + QualityScoreBreakdown + scoreBand, with 11 tests. Nothing is recomputed client-side (AC5 forbids it) — the component consumes the score the edge already returns on /listings/validate. Design points, each test-pinned: blocked is its OWN colour band and renders "Can not list" instead of a number, because painting a blocked listing the same amber as a weak-but-listable one would undo on screen the very sort-ordering the server-side cap exists to create; an unscored listing renders an em dash, never 0 (NULL and 0 are different facts); an unknown component shows "not checked" rather than 0/10, matching the server excluding it from the maths; a Fix action appears only for genuinely fixable components; and the breakdown states "Scored on N of 100 points" when weightCounted < 100 so partial information is admitted rather than passed off as a full assessment. Negative-verified: removing the blocked band, and rendering 0 for unscored, each turn the suite red. STILL OPEN for passes: wiring the chip into the drafts list + pipeline board (needs those pages routing a fixSurface handler), and AC5 iOS. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AC2 DRAFTS-LIST WIRING DONE. autolister-drafts.tsx renders the QualityScoreChip per row and gains a "Quality: low first" sort. ⚠ THE IMPORTANT DETAIL: the score is fetched in a SEPARATE, FAIL-SOFT query, not added to the existing drafts select. That query does "if (error) throw error", so adding quality_score to it would 42703 and take the WHOLE DRAFTS PAGE DOWN the moment the frontend deploys ahead of migration 00476 — the exact hazard CLAUDE.md’s held-migration rule warns about for client-side reads of a new column. With a separate query a missing column just means no chips, and every draft honestly reads "not scored". The two judgement calls were extracted to src/pages/flipdesk/draft-quality.ts so they are testable without rendering the page (the repo’s status-param-to-tab.ts pattern): scoreMapFromRows OMITS a NULL quality_score rather than coercing it to 0 (never-scored and scored-zero are different facts, and a 0 would both render a confident chip and sort an unscored draft in with the genuinely worst), and qualityRankOf sinks unscored drafts to the END of the worst-first sort ("we do not know" is not evidence of low quality; floating unknowns to the top would bury the listings we DO know are weak, defeating the sort). 6 helper tests + 11 component tests; the sinks-to-end rule negative-verified by inverting it (2 tests go red). Full web suite 162 files / 2162 tests green, lint exit 0, tsc clean. REMAINING for passes: the pipeline board surface (AC2 names drafts list AND pipeline board) and AC5 iOS. | 2026-07-18 PIPELINE-BOARD SURFACE SCOPED (not built — there is a real design question first). The drafts cockpit was straightforward because it queries `listings` directly, so the persisted quality_score is a column on the row it already renders. pipeline.tsx queries `inventory_items` instead, and an item can have SEVERAL listings (a draft plus a live one, or historical ended rows). So 'the item's quality score' is ambiguous: newest listing? the draft? the live one? worst of them? Each answer changes what a worst-first sort means on that board, and picking one silently is how a number ends up meaning different things on two screens. DECIDE FIRST, then wire — the mechanics are already proven (fail-soft separate query keyed by inventory_item_id + QualityScoreChip + qualityRankOf, per the drafts-list commit). Deliberately not guessed at, since US-1897 cannot close anyway while AC5 needs a macOS session. | 2026-07-18 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop, prompted by prd-lint findStaleHeldMigrations): the HELD language above is OBSOLETE and is superseded by this note — the migration file is already on origin/main, so the branch is NOT frozen and nobody should hold a push on its account. The distinction the old wording blurs and that still matters: PUSHED is not APPLIED. The file being on origin/main says nothing about whether the SQL has run against the prod DB; PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md remains the source of truth for what is actually applied, and 00475/00476 are still listed there as genuinely pending. So the correct residual action is an APPLY (+ NOTIFY pgrst), not a push-hold. | 2026-07-18 MEASURED CORRECTION to the status note above (agent loop): I wrote earlier today that "PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md remains the source of truth ... 00475/00476 are still listed there as genuinely pending". That is FALSE and I am correcting my own claim. GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns schema {expected:00476, applied:00476, status:match} — the US-1566 block reading applied_migrations through the service-role client, i.e. the DB own answer. 00475 and 00476 ARE APPLIED in prod. The only genuinely pending migration is 00477 (US-1999, correctly held/unpushed). PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md has been corrected with the measured evidence and both sections re-marked APPLIED. The lesson: the answer was one unauthenticated HTTP GET away the whole time, and several passes (including mine) reasoned about prod schema state from commit history instead of measuring it.

userStories.title: Stale-listing playbook: traffic-based revise suggestions (never auto-relist)
userStories.description: As a seller, I want listings with weeks of zero engagement surfaced with concrete revise-in-place suggestions (price vs comps, weak title, missing photos), because eBay's search team confirmed end-and-relist destroys accumulated performance data — the right move is real changes to the live listing. Audit: no traffic data is pulled today; relist exists but nothing guides when/what to change instead.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge syncs per-listing impressions/clicks/watchers via the Sell Analytics getTrafficReport API into a listing_traffic table (cron, cadence documented; tenant-scoped per US-268 with a tenant-isolation test case)

A 'stale' surface (pipeline filter or dedicated view) lists live GT-origin listings with N days of zero clicks (default 45, configurable), each with suggested actions ranked by the Quality Score breakdown (US-1897) + comp-band price check — every action routes through revise-in-place (US-1490)
Explicitly NO auto end/relist anywhere in this flow; 'Sell Similar' is offered only as a manual last resort for 90+ day zero-engagement listings, with copy explaining the tradeoff
Traffic columns visible on the listings table for sorting; deno tests cover the staleness query + tenant scoping
userStories.notes: [P3][SEO][Edge] See EBAY_RANKING_PLAYBOOK.md §5. New cron: remember the edge-image curl gotcha + Coolify scheduled-task registration. Load tenant-isolation skill for the new route/table. Added 2026-07-09.

userStories.title: RLS policies never wrap auth.uid() / workspace-member helper in a scalar subquery → per-row re-evaluation on large reads
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want per-user reads to stay fast at scale. Grep shows 178 `USING/WITH CHECK` clauses calling bare `auth.uid()` and zero using the `(select auth.uid())` initplan form Supabase recommends. For the ~28 child-table policies using correlated `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM parent WHERE ... = auth.uid())` (submission_images, item_photos, grade_reports, shipments, ...) the planner re-runs the subquery per candidate row. Separately, the listings/sales/inventory policies (00146) call `is_workspace_member_with_role(user_id, 'viewer')` — a SECURITY DEFINER function whose STABLE caching only collapses same-`user_id` calls, so a cross-tenant scan re-invokes it (and its workspace_members lookup) per distinct owner.
acceptanceCriteria: High-traffic per-user policies rewritten to `USING ((select auth.uid()) = user_id)` (and equivalents) so the planner hoists to a single initplan; prioritize the correlated-subquery child tables

A supporting index on `workspace_members(workspace_owner_id, member_user_id, role)` exists; the `is_workspace_member_with_role` helper short-circuits the owner case before querying, and callers pre-filter by `user_id`
EXPLAIN (or the supabase-postgres-best-practices lane) confirms the initplan form on a representative large per-user SELECT; migration follows the US-1108 triple
Load the `supabase-postgres-best-practices` and `migrations` skills
userStories.notes: [P2][DB/Perf] Code-review sweep 2026-07-11. Combines two related planner findings. Load `supabase-postgres-best-practices` + `migrations` skills. | 2026-07-15 (branch cursor/measurements-ebay-live-sync): CODE COMPLETE, HELD — migration 00451_rls_initplan_perf.sql. Rewrote the hot-path per-user RLS to the Supabase initplan form ((select auth.uid())) + gave every workspace-member-helper policy a cheap owner fast-path disjunct ((select auth.uid()) = user_id OR is_workspace_member...) so the SECURITY DEFINER helper is never CALLED for owner rows on a single-tenant scan (AC1). Tables: submissions, submission_images, grade_reports, inventory_items, listings, sales, shipments, item_photos (owner + workspace policies each). CREATE OR REPLACEd is_workspace_member/_with_role (internal auth.uid()->(select auth.uid()), owner OR-branch kept as short-circuit) + added covering index idx_workspace_members_owner_member_role (owner_id, member_id, role) (AC2). US-1108 triple done: idempotent DROP-IF-EXISTS+CREATE, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 00451 same commit, self-record footer. Edge tests green (schema-version sync + rls-guard). HELD migration: apply to prod + NOTIFY pgrst before pushing (see PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md). | 2026-07-18 STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop): the 'HELD migration: apply to prod + NOTIFY pgrst before pushing' instruction above is STALE and should not be acted on. 00451_rls_initplan_perf.sql is on origin/main, and prod's applied schema version is proven to be >= 00474 (the deployed edge expects 00474 and a confirmed-behind DB hard-exits at boot; the latest_schema_migration RPC exists — it returns 42501 permission denied to anon, not PGRST202 not-found — so the guard's version read cannot be failing open). 00451 <= 00474, so AC1/AC2's DDL is applied in production and this story is NOT waiting on an apply or a push. userStories.title: Public /cert/:id certificate pages 404 in production — the verify-a-grade trust chain is dead
userStories.description: As a buyer, we want every published grade certificate at /cert/:id to render, so a buyer can verify a grade before paying. In production (2026-07-13) every /cert/<uuid> linked off the live Verified Seller profile /verified/pearson returns HTTP 404 serving the BLOG's not-found body ('That post doesn't exist... Back to the blog') — confirmed across 16+ real cert IDs by two independent QA personas. A made-up cert id returns the IDENTICAL 404, so a buyer cannot distinguish a genuine certificate from a forgery. The Pages Function functions/cert/[id].ts exists and /cert/* IS in public/_routes.json, so this is a deploy/runtime failure (Function erroring then Pages fallback, or prod cert-lookup/migration drift), NOT a missing route. This breaks the core product promise ('a certificate buyers can verify'). SECONDARY: /verify tells buyers to look for 'Cert #GT-7K2M9'-style codes (src/lib/cert-number.ts) but the actual cert artifacts/URLs are raw UUIDs, so the code a buyer is told to find does not appear on the cert.
acceptanceCriteria: /cert/<valid-id> renders the full certificate (grade + five-factor breakdown + date + methodology version + confidence + tamper-evident check) in production for real published certs from /verified/pearson

An INVALID or nonexistent cert id returns a distinct, cert-branded 'certificate not found / could not be verified' page — never the blog 404 and never byte-identical to a valid cert's error, so genuine vs forged is distinguishable
Root cause identified and documented (deploy emitted the Function / prod cert lookup works); a post-deploy smoke check asserts /cert/<seeded-id> returns 200
The homepage sample-certificate card links to a real, working seeded certificate (currently it is not a link)
Reconcile the advertised 'Cert #GT-XXXXX' format (cert-number.ts) with the cert identity actually shown on the page/URL
userStories.notes: [P1][Web/SSR][Blocker] 5-persona QA sweep 2026-07-13. Cert 404 independently confirmed by the buyer-auditor and vintage-seller personas across 16+ real IDs off /verified/pearson; blog-branded 404 body + /cert/* present in _routes.json means Function deploy/runtime failure, not a missing route. Likely relates to functions-not-typechecked-by-build and/or prod-migration-drift. Treat as a LAUNCH BLOCKER — the entire 'verifiable certificate' value prop is non-functional in prod. Needs prod deploy verification (cannot be reproduced on local build alone). PARTIAL 2026-07-13 (local main, NOT pushed — Pages Function change; deploys on push). LOCAL FIX DONE: notFoundResponse() was blog-hardcoded ("That post doesn't exist... Back to the blog") and reused by ALL 9 dynamic SSR Functions (cert, verified-seller, passport, condition-index, value, durability, authors, blog) — so a missing CERT told buyers to go back to the blog. Refactored to a generic default + per-caller copy; the cert Function now returns a DISTINCT cert-branded "Certificate not found" page (satisfies the genuine-vs-forged AC). functions tsc -p tsconfig.functions.json clean. ROOT CAUSE of valid certs 404ing (still OPEN, PROD-SIDE): the cert Function + edge endpoint GET /certificates/:id (content-public.ts:581) are correct in code; the endpoint returns empty in prod. isCertificateWithheld ruled out (only withholds pending_review/flagged-unapproved). Prime suspect: prod-migration-drift — a column in CERT_REPORT_COLUMNS missing in prod makes the grade_reports select error -> publicError -> cert 404 (matches the prod-migration-drift memory). Also check EDGE_API_URL in the Pages env. HANDOFF DIAGNOSTIC: curl https://functions.gradethread.com/api/content/public/certificates/<real-id from /verified/pearson> — a 5xx/40x or {error:query} confirms the endpoint; then re-apply idempotent migrations for grade_reports + NOTIFY pgrst, or fix the Pages EDGE_API_URL. Remaining ACs needing prod/data: seed VITE_SAMPLE_CERTIFICATE_ID to a real public cert for the homepage sample link. userStories.title: bulkMigrateListing — bring a seller's existing eBay (Trading) listings under management
userStories.description: As an established reseller onboarding to GradeThread, I want to manage my existing eBay listings, not just view them. Today Trading-created listings import read-only (getAllActiveEbaySelling) and relist explicitly refuses eBay-origin, so a new customer's live catalog can never be revised/repriced/promoted through GradeThread — a major onboarding wall. Implement Inventory API bulk_migrate_listing to convert eligible legacy listings into managed Inventory offers.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge calls POST /sell/inventory/v1/bulk_migrate_listing for eligible active Trading listings and links the resulting SKU/offerId to the inventory_items/listings rows
Migrated listings flip to a managed origin so revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote become available (respecting the sync source-of-truth contract)
Ineligible listings (variations/other) are reported with the eBay reason, not silently dropped
Idempotent; a seller can trigger migration from the app and see progress/results
userStories.notes: [P2][Edge/Inventory] iOS listing-lifecycle audit 2026-07-14. No bulkMigrateListing anywhere; relist refuses origin==='ebay' (flipdesk-ebay.ts:6503). See SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md — migration changes a mirror into a GT-managed listing. Unlocks managing existing catalogs (most customers' day one). | INVESTIGATION 2026-07-17 (no code): AC2's PROMISE WOULD BE SILENTLY FALSE without an unstated design decision. GOOD NEWS FIRST: AC2's 'flip to a managed origin' needs NO migration — listing_origin is already an enum with both values (00232) and deriveListingOrigin() lets a persisted marker WIN over the provenance signals (sync-precedence.ts:330), so setting listing_origin='gradethread' does unlock revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote. THE PROBLEM IS THE SKU. bulkMigrateListing returns eBay's OWN sku + offerId per listing (inventoryItems[{sku,offerId}], max 5 listings/call, per-listing statusCode + errors[] — verified against eBay docs). The Inventory API keys EVERYTHING on that sku. But nothing in GradeThread stores a per-listing sku: BOTH the publish path (flipdesk-ebay.ts:8733) and the revise/list path (:9450) DERIVE it as (item.sku)?.trim() || 'FD-'+id.slice(0,8). So if eBay's migrated sku differs from our derived one — likely, since eBay derives it from the listing's Custom Label or generates it — then after a 'successful' migration every subsequent GT Inventory call targets an inventory item that does not exist, and revise/reprice/withdraw all fail. The listing would be marked GT-managed while being unmanageable: strictly worse than the read-only mirror it replaced, because the origin flip ALSO stops the inbound pull from mirroring it (SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH: EBAY_OWNED_LISTING_FIELDS are only overwritten while origin='ebay'). So the row would go stale AND be unmanageable. THE DECISION (needed before implementing): where does eBay's migrated sku live? (a) listings.platform_fields.migrated_sku — jsonb exists (00113), NO migration, but both sku-deriving sites must learn to prefer it; (b) overwrite inventory_items.sku with eBay's — there IS precedent (ebay-sku-match.tsx:983 already writes eBay's Custom Label into item.sku 'so the two systems agree'), and it is user-initiated rather than a pull, BUT SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH lists sku under GRADETHREAD_OWNED_ITEM_FIELDS ('always owned by GradeThread — no eBay pull may write these') and item.sku is unique-per-user so a migrated sku can COLLIDE with an existing item; (c) a new listings.platform_sku column — cleanest, needs a MIGRATION (blocked while the agent loop consumes 00468-00473 for the Brand KB block). Recommend (c), or (a) if the migration must wait. This is a documented-contract decision (CLAUDE.md flags SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md as the contract for this area), not a coin flip — deliberately not decided unilaterally. Everything else about the story is ready: eBay's contract is confirmed, the origin flip works, and the flip must happen ONLY after eBay confirms the per-listing migration succeeded (a partial failure must leave origin='ebay', or the row becomes stale AND unmanageable). BLOCKED ON US-1999 (filed 2026-07-18). The SKU problem this note identified is not specific to migration — it is a live defect in its own right: the eBay Inventory SKU is derived at three sites from the freely-editable inventory_items.sku and never pinned, so a seller renaming a SKU can orphan an already-live listing. US-1999 adds the stored SKU. Migration cannot link bulk_migrate_listing's returned sku to anything until that column exists, so do US-1999 first and this story gets much smaller. | 2026-07-18 EDGE COMPLETE (agent loop) — THE BLOCKER IS GONE. The 2026-07-17 investigation ended on an open design question (where does eBay own migrated sku live?); US-1999 answered it this session by adding listings.inventory_sku (00477), so option (a) platform_fields.migrated_sku is moot — the SKU has a real, indexed, listing-scoped column and BOTH derive sites already read it. AC1 — lib/ebay-migrate.ts (pure) + bulkMigrateListing() in ebay-client.ts + POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate. AC2 — the origin flip and the SKU write happen in ONE update and ONLY when eBay returned a SKU; the module header and a dedicated test spell out why: flipping origin without the sku produces a row that is marked managed, is not addressable by any Inventory call, AND has stopped being refreshed by the inbound pull (SYNC_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH only overwrites EBAY_OWNED_LISTING_FIELDS while origin=ebay) — strictly worse than the mirror it replaced. The single most important test asserts a 2xx WITH NO SKU is a FAILURE, not a success. AC3 — every listing is accounted for: eBay errors surface longMessage verbatim; listings eBay omitted from responses[] are reported rather than vanishing; and OUR OWN pre-flight skips (not found / already GT-published / no platform_listing_id / not active) each carry a reason, since a listing that silently disappears from the result is the same defect whether we or eBay dropped it. AC4 (partial) — idempotent: an already-migrated row returns already_managed instead of erroring, so retrying a partly-failed batch is safe; eBay 5-per-call cap enforced by chunkForMigrate, plus a separate 50-per-REQUEST cap so one HTTP call cannot fan out into 40 sequential eBay calls and time out. US-268: ids come from the request body, so the read is scoped .eq(user_id, workspaceOwnerId ?? userId) and only rows that come back are acted on; a request naming ONLY foreign ids 404s rather than returning 200 with per-item not-found (a bulk 200 would make a cross-tenant probe indistinguishable from success at the status level), and tenant-isolation_test.ts has the required case. Verified: deno check + lint clean, 4144 edge tests pass (8 new). ⚠ HELD — depends on 00477, so it ships with that migration; the route SELECTs inventory_sku. STILL OPEN for passes: AC4 UI (trigger + progress/results in the app — the Reconciliation page is the natural home) and a real-eBay end-to-end run, which cannot be done in the sandbox. | 2026-07-18 AC4 UI DONE (agent loop). Trigger + per-listing results now live in the app. Placement is deliberate: the button sits IN the amber "this listing was created on eBay, so eBay owns its title/price/description/photos" banner on the item canvas — the exact place the seller hits the wall — rather than on a settings page they would have to know to look for. useMigrateEbayListings() reports eBay reasons PER LISTING rather than collapsing to one "done" (a multi-variation rejection is actionable, "failed" is not), capped at 3 toasts so a large batch cannot bury the screen. ⚠ FOUND AND FIXED A DEFECT THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THE WHOLE FEATURE LOOK BROKEN: item-canvas computed lockedByEbay via deriveListingOrigin() but its listings query never SELECTED listing_origin — and that persisted column is exactly what migration writes, and what deriveListingOrigin lets WIN over the provenance signals. So post-migration the row still had a platform_listing_id, no batch_id and no synced_to_ebay_at, the canvas would have re-derived "ebay", and the seller would have seen the locked banner and the migrate button still sitting there after a SUCCESSFUL migration. Added listing_origin to the select + the two type literals, and invalidated the item_ebay_sync query in the mutation (it backs that banner; without it the UI would not refetch at all). Pinned with a NEW test file src/lib/__tests__/listing-origin.test.ts — deriveListingOrigin gates revise/reprice/withdraw/relist/promote and the locked-fields banner across the app and had ZERO test coverage before this; 5 tests now cover persisted-marker-wins (both directions), unrecognized-marker fallback, batch/sync signals, draft-with-no-listing-id, and non-eBay platforms. Verified: tsc -b clean, eslint 0 errors, 2232 vitest tests pass, 4144 deno tests pass. STILL passes:false — the only thing left is a real-eBay end-to-end run (publish a Trading listing, migrate it, then revise/reprice it), which cannot be done from the sandbox. Everything code-side across all four ACs is complete. Still HELD behind 00477. | 2026-07-18 STALE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM — STATUS CORRECTION (agent loop): the HELD language above is OBSOLETE. The stack was pushed and BOTH migrations are APPLIED IN PRODUCTION — measured, not assumed: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns schema {expected:00478, applied:00478, status:match} with database ok and status ready, and the deployed frontend bundle reports release 91d466d22f2ef6061e07d6dd56f2a521a5aa562a (the head of origin/main). So the apply-before-push ordering was honored and nothing is frozen. Post-deploy smoke checks run the same day: POST /api/flipdesk/ebay/listings/migrate returns 401 (auth enforced) rather than a 42703 column-does-not-exist, which is the specific failure that would indicate 00477 had not landed; a real certificate off sitemap-certs.xml still returns 200, so the grading/cert path is unbroken; and gradethread.com now serves Permissions-Policy camera=(self) (a first check showed the old camera=() from a cached response — the cache-busted request confirmed the fix is live, worth noting because that cached read looked exactly like a failed deploy).

userStories.title: eBay Media API: video upload for listings
userStories.description: As a clothing seller, I want to add video to my listings to lift conversion. Today images are passed as external URLs only (InventoryItemPayload.imageUrls) and there is no video support. Integrate the eBay Media API (/commerce/media) to upload video and attach it to listings.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge can createVideo -> uploadVideo -> poll getVideo to a terminal status, and attach the resulting id via product.videoIds on createOrReplaceInventoryItem

TRANSCODE DECISION MADE AND WRITTEN DOWN: eBay accepts .mp4 H.264/AVC only, and iPhones record HEVC by default. Either the client transcodes before upload, or the edge does, or HEVC is rejected with a message that tells the seller how to fix it. Silently failing on the most common input is not an option

PUBLISH-ORDERING DECISION MADE: processing is async and terminal status is not immediate, so either publish waits for LIVE, or publish proceeds without video and a later revise attaches it. Whichever is chosen, a seller never ends up with a listing that permanently lacks the video they added
BLOCKED is handled as a moderation outcome, not an error: it is terminal and expected, and the seller is told their video was rejected rather than shown a retry that cannot succeed
Video upload gets its own validation path. The US-276 hardening (validateImageUpload / stripImageMetadata) is image-only and does NOT cover video, which also carries GPS/EXIF-equivalent metadata
iOS/web can add a video during compose and see it reflected on the published listing
Respects the Media API POST rate limit (50 requests / 5 seconds, per user)
userStories.notes:
[P3][Edge/Media] iOS listing-lifecycle audit 2026-07-14. No Media API; images external-URL only (InventoryItemPayload.imageUrls). Nice-to-have; video is a real apparel conversion lever. 

INVESTIGATED 2026-07-18. Confirmed greenfield: no videoId / commerce-media / uploadVideo reference anywhere in services/edge-functions/src or src. Two findings change the shape of this story.

FINDING 1 — NOT SCOPE-BLOCKED, contrary to the obvious assumption. The Media API's createVideo requires sell.inventory, which is ALREADY in our production grant (ebay-client.ts:233). This story therefore does NOT depend on US-1421 (restricted-scope acquisition) and does not need a new seller consent round. Attachment is also on the path we already use: product.videoIds on createOrReplaceInventoryItem — a sibling of the product.imageUrls we already send at ebay-client.ts:2163 — NOT a Trading-API-only feature as the AddItem/VideoDetails docs might suggest. So the integration surface is much smaller than the P3 implies: the eBay side is three new calls plus one extra field on a payload we already build.

FINDING 2 — THE REAL COST IS TRANSCODING, AND IT LANDS ON AC2. eBay accepts .mp4 MPEG-4 Part 10 / AVC (H.264) only. iPhones have defaulted to HEVC / H.265 since iOS 11 unless the user changed Camera > Formats to 'Most Compatible'. AC2 specifically promises iOS compose. So the single most likely real-world input is a format eBay will not accept, and the failure would surface late — after upload, as PROCESSING_FAILED — which is the worst place to discover it. Whoever picks this up should size the transcode decision FIRST, because it dominates the estimate: client-side transcode, server-side transcode (ffmpeg in the Deno container, which is a real image-size and CPU change on Coolify), or explicit rejection. The eBay calls are the easy part.

FLOW: createVideo returns 201 with the video id in the Location header -> uploadVideo sends the bytes -> poll getVideo. Statuses PENDING_UPLOAD -> PROCESSING -> LIVE, with BLOCKED and PROCESSING_FAILED as the other terminal states. BLOCKED is a moderation verdict rather than a fault, so it needs its own message; a generic retry there loops forever. Rate limit is 50 POSTs / 5s per user.

ALSO: AC3's original wording ('routes through the hardened fetch path') is misleading and has been rewritten. Our upload hardening is image-specific — validateImageUpload magic-byte-sniffs for images and stripImageMetadata drops EXIF/GPS from images. Neither does anything for an .mp4, which carries its own location metadata. Video needs a parallel validator, not a reuse of the image one.

NOT CONFIRMED, flagged rather than guessed: max file size, max duration, and how many videos a single listing accepts. eBay's docs point at Seller Center for those numbers and I could not retrieve them (developer.ebay.com WebFetch timed out twice; the above is from eBay doc search summaries, not the doc pages read directly). Confirm those three numbers against the live docs before implementing, since max-duration in particular shapes the compose UX.

userStories.title: US-1891 backwards title sync never shipped server-side — the edge title-sync module has zero callers
userStories.description: As a seller, when I correct an item's Brand/size/color/style/department from ANY surface, I want the listing title to update — not just from the web item canvas. US-1891 (P1, archived passes:true) required the substitution on 'the edge item update path AND web item-canvas save' (its AC2). Only the web half shipped. src/lib/title-sync.ts is wired into item-canvas.tsx persist(); its declared lockstep mirror services/edge-functions/src/lib/title-sync.ts is imported by NOTHING — verified 2026-07-18, every export has zero production references. So an edit made through the edge item-update API, iOS, AutoLister, bulk edit or CSV import still corrects the brand and leaves the OLD brand in listing_title: exactly the bug US-1891 exists to fix, on every surface except one. Both suites are green because each calls its own copy directly, so nothing signals the gap.
acceptanceCriteria: Item edits from EVERY non-canvas write path apply the same substitution the web canvas does, under the same conditions (GT-origin non-ebay listings only; both title_variants; hand-edited-vs-ai_generated_snapshot sets needs_review; live listings queue the revise-in-place prompt, never end/relist). NOTE: there is no generic edge item-update endpoint — see the 2026-07-18 scope correction; the concrete surfaces are web bulk-edit (brand/size/color/style, nearest gap), identification-verify, and iOS
It cannot DOUBLE-APPLY against the frontend path — decide one owner per surface, or make the substitution provably idempotent for the web canvas case that already ran it

iOS is the ONLY remaining surface (audited 2026-07-18): AIItemFieldWriter.swift writes brand/size/color/style and iOS never writes listing_title. identification-verify only annotates provenance, and CSV import is fill-only so a blank old value makes the substitution a provable no-op — neither needs wiring. Needs a macOS session; test the Swift port against src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json so it cannot drift from the two JS copies

A BEHAVIOURAL parity fixture shared by both suites: one table of (title, field changes) -> expected output asserted by the deno test AND the vitest test, so the two copies cannot drift. They currently differ by ~80 lines and nothing pins them — the frontend inlines the trim because it cannot import title-trim.ts across projects, which is legitimate, but that is exactly why source-diffing cannot be the guard
The ⚠ block at the top of the edge title-sync.ts is removed once it has real callers
userStories.notes: [P1][Sync/SEO][Regression of an ARCHIVED story] Found 2026-07-18 by the unwired-export audit that also produced US-1994. This is the more serious of the two: US-1994 is a contract divergence with no known live bug, whereas this is a P1 feature that measurably does not run on most surfaces. US-1891's own notes describe the web wiring in detail ('Wired into item-canvas persist()') and never claim the edge half — the AC asked for both, and the story was marked done anyway. Worth asking what else in the archive has the same shape: a 'lockstep mirror' is a strong smell, since only one copy usually gets a caller. Do NOT just import the module in an edge route and call it — see AC2/AC3; the double-apply and needs_review semantics are the hard part, not the substitution. Meanwhile the edge module carries a ⚠ header naming the gap so its green tests stop reading as proof the feature works server-side. | 2026-07-18 (cont.): the audit is now a repeatable tool — scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs. Re-running it correctly found 10 WHOLE MODULES that no production file imports, carrying 143 test references between them: drip-trigger.ts (4 exports/31 refs — US-933s unified trigger engine, SUPERSEDED by the inline switch(journey.trigger) in jobs-journey-tick.ts, so dead rather than broken), title-sync.ts (4/29 — this story), authenticity-eval.ts (6/24), measure-eval-stats.ts (3/16 — the MeasureCard accuracy gate, plausibly just pending its OPEN story US-1582), ai-size-estimate-core.ts (3/15), brand-seed.ts (2/12), grading-reliability.ts (2/11), grade-badge.ts (1/5), content-ai-email.ts (4/0), rubric.ts (1/0). Each needs verifying by hand: superseded, pending, and half-wired all look identical to the tool. NOTE the tool initially MISSED title-sync.ts — the module that motivated it — because its exports call each other (syncTitle uses applyTitleSubstitution), so per-function reference counting read internal cohesion as reachability. Whole-module deadness is now decided by the IMPORT GRAPH, which is the only signal that cannot be faked from inside the module. | 2026-07-18 SCOPE CORRECTED — MY OWN FRAMING WAS WRONG. This story (and its first AC) assumed 'the edge item update path' exists. IT DOES NOT: there is no generic item-update endpoint anywhere in services/edge-functions — no route does .update() on inventory_items. Anyone picking this up would have started by hunting for an endpoint that was never built. WHAT ACTUALLY WRITES ITEM FIELDS (verified 2026-07-18): (1) web item-canvas.tsx — a DIRECT supabase write, no edge round-trip, and the ONLY surface that runs title-sync; (2) web autolister-bulk-edit.tsx:872 — also a direct supabase .update(), and it patches brand/size/color/style, i.e. FOUR OF THE FIVE SYNCABLE_TITLE_FIELDS, with NO title sync at all; (3) edge lib/ai-listing.ts:1793 and lib/grading-pipeline.ts:657 — but US-1891's notes state the AI-apply path REGENERATES titles wholesale so it deliberately needs no sync; (4) edge lib/identification-verify.ts:245 (attributes); (5) iOS. SO THE HEADLINE CHANGES: the nearest, cheapest gap is NOT iOS or the edge — it is WEB BULK EDIT, in the same codebase, with src/lib/title-sync.ts already sitting there importable. A seller who bulk-corrects a brand across 40 drafts gets 40 stale titles, and that is the exact bug US-1891 was written to kill. AND THE REAL QUESTION IS ARCHITECTURAL, not a wiring task: with writes distributed across five+ surfaces in three languages, per-surface mirrors do not converge — that is how there came to be two copies of title-sync with only one wired. The decision to make FIRST is WHERE THE INVARIANT LIVES: a DB trigger on inventory_items (fires for every writer, including iOS and any future one), funnelling item writes through a single edge endpoint (large change, but kills the whole class), or accepting per-surface mirrors with a shared behavioural fixture as the guard. Do not start coding before that is settled. The AC list above still stands EXCEPT AC1's 'edge item update path' phrasing, which should be read as 'every non-canvas write path'. | SIZING THE BULK-EDIT GAP (same pass): it is smaller than it looks. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx ALREADY selects listing_title AND ai_generated_snapshot from listings (line ~190) — which are exactly the two inputs title-sync needs, ai_generated_snapshot being the hand-edited-vs-AI check that decides whether to set needs_review — and it ALREADY writes back to listings (line ~707). It imports title-sync zero times; item-canvas.tsx imports it three. So IF the chosen answer is per-surface mirrors, this specific fix is roughly 'call changesFromItemDiff + syncTitle in the existing patch loop', not a new data path. I DELIBERATELY DID NOT MAKE THAT CHANGE. This same note argues scattered per-surface call sites are the disease — two copies of title-sync with one wired — so adding a fifth call site before the where-does-the-invariant-live decision would be inconsistent with the advice above, and wasted work if the answer turns out to be a DB trigger on inventory_items (which would cover iOS and every future writer for free). The sizing is recorded so whoever makes the call knows the per-surface option is cheap, not so the decision gets skipped. | 2026-07-18 ARCHITECTURE DECIDED + AC4 DONE. THE DECISION: per-surface mirrors with a shared BEHAVIOURAL fixture — NOT a DB trigger. I had earlier offered the trigger as my pick and then argued myself out of it: applyTitleSubstitution is 100+ lines of token-boundary, case-transfer, multi-word-brand and size-pattern string handling, so porting it to plpgsql would create a THIRD implementation in the language with the worst string handling of the three. That is a bigger version of the disease, not a cure. Funnelling every item write through one edge endpoint was also rejected for now: item writes are direct supabase calls from multiple clients (web canvas, web bulk-edit, iOS), so that is a large migration of its own and does not have to be paid before fixing the actual bug. AC4 SHIPPED: src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json — 13 cases (10 syncTitle + 3 changesFromItemDiff) read by BOTH suites, services/edge-functions/src/tests/title-sync_test.ts and src/lib/__tests__/title-sync.test.ts. A source diff could never have been the guard: the two files legitimately differ by ~80 lines because the web copy inlines the trim (it cannot import title-trim.ts across projects). Behaviour is the only thing that can be compared. FINDING: the two copies currently AGREE on all 13 cases — I ran the fixture against each implementation before wiring it in, so a disagreement would have surfaced as data rather than as a red test I then rationalised. So they had not behaviourally drifted; the risk was that nothing would have caught it if they did. Negative-verified: breaking case-transfer in the web copy alone turns 3 web tests red naming the exact fixture case, and the edge suite stays green (which is the point — the failing side identifies itself). Verified: edge 4129 passed / 0 failed, web 2164 passed, tsc clean, lint exit 0. STILL OPEN: the actual gap. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx patches brand/size/color/style with no title sync, and it already loads listing_title + ai_generated_snapshot and already writes to listings — so with the fixture now guarding the copies, wiring that call site is the next step and is safe to take. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) THE BULK-EDIT GAP IS CLOSED. autolister-bulk-edit.tsx now syncs the listing title when its reverse-projection writes brand/size/color/style back onto the item — so a seller who bulk-corrects a brand across 40 drafts no longer gets 40 titles still naming the old one. I did NOT inline item-canvas's ~30 lines of orchestration, which would have been a FOURTH copy — of the orchestration this time, the substitution already being shared. Extracted it instead to src/lib/title-sync-patch.ts: buildTitleSyncPatch is pure (inputs -> listings patch, no IO) and owns the decisions wrapped around syncTitle — refuse ebay-origin listings (the sync-precedence guard), move BOTH A/B variants, and flag needs_review when the title was hand-edited away from ai_generated_snapshot or the listing is live. 9 unit tests. That extraction is the actual fix for this story's root cause: the pure helper was shared and the ORCHESTRATION was not, which is why only one surface ever ran it. NOTE the guard is explicit, not inherited: this page filters batch_id + listing_status='draft', which implies GradeThread origin via deriveListingOrigin, but relying on that implicit invariant is how these contracts rot — listing_origin is now selected and checked directly (the column has existed since 00232, far below prod's >=00474, so unlike quality_score it is safe to read). TYPESCRIPT CAUGHT A REAL BUG MID-WIRING: I threaded the new columns onto DraftRow but the save loop iterates EditRow, a different shape — tsc flagged four property errors rather than letting it fail at runtime on undefined. Fixed by carrying listingOrigin/titleVariants through the EditRow mapping. Verified: web suite 2173 passed (was 2164), tsc clean, lint exit 0. REMAINING for passes: the OTHER non-canvas surfaces — identification-verify (edge) and iOS — plus confirming CSV import routes through a covered path. Those are separate surfaces, not this one; buildTitleSyncPatch is deliberately pure so the edge and a future iOS port can consume the same decisions rather than re-deriving them. item-canvas.tsx should also be refactored onto it (it still has the longhand version) — mechanical, but it touches a large working component so it wants its own change. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) item-canvas.tsx REFACTORED onto buildTitleSyncPatch, so the orchestration now exists ONCE in the web app. I had created a second copy in the previous commit by extracting the helper for bulk-edit while leaving the canvas's longhand in place — which is the same duplication this story exists to remove, so leaving it would have been incoherent. ~30 lines of inline logic replaced by one Object.assign; tsc then flagged syncTitle and trimTitleToLimit as unused imports in that file, which is the tidy confirmation that the longhand path is genuinely gone rather than merely bypassed. PROVED BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING BEFORE COMMITTING, not asserted: transcribed the OLD inline block verbatim into a throwaway test and compared it against buildTitleSyncPatch across the full input matrix — locked/unlocked x 4 change-sets x 4 titles (incl. empty, over-long-so-pure-retrim, and a token-boundary near-miss) x 3 variant shapes (incl. null entries) x 4 snapshot states x live/not = 768 combinations, 0 mismatches. Same standard as the 2048-subset proof used for US-1994's route swap. The throwaway was deleted after it passed; the durable coverage is title-sync-patch.test.ts (9 cases) plus the shared edge<->web fixture. Verified: web suite 2173 passed, tsc clean, lint exit 0. | 2026-07-18 REMAINING SURFACES AUDITED — three of the four need NO work, and the scope is now exactly ONE surface (iOS). Evidence per surface rather than assumption: (1) identification-verify.ts (edge) — NOT APPLICABLE. It updates only { attributes, ai_field_sources }, and the attributes it writes spread the existing map and add just identification_verified + market_title_keywords. Neither is a SYNCABLE_TITLE_FIELD, so it never changes a value a title could contain; it annotates provenance/confidence, it does not re-identify the garment. (2) CSV import (src/pages/flipdesk/import.tsx) — NOT APPLICABLE, for a subtler reason worth writing down. It is FILL-ONLY (isBlank(existing[field]) && !isBlank(incoming)), so it can only populate a brand that was previously blank. A blank old value means there is nothing in the title to substitute: syncTitle with a blank `from` is a deliberate no-op, pinned by the shared fixture case 'blank from/to is ignored rather than blanking the title'. Filling a blank brand cannot fix a title that never named one, so wiring sync here would add a call that provably does nothing. Its own comment also confirms 'Listings/sales are left untouched on re-import'. (3) iOS — GENUINE REMAINING GAP, and the only one. ios/GradeThread/AIExtract/AIItemFieldWriter.swift writes brand/size/color/style to inventory_items via a sparse FieldUpdate, and it is NOT fill-only: it keeps a Snapshot of pre-fill values expressly so an undo can restore them, which only matters if the write can overwrite a populated column. A repo-wide grep shows iOS NEVER writes listing_title anywhere. So an AI-fill on iOS that corrects a brand updates the item column and leaves the listing title naming the old one — the original US-1891 bug, surviving on exactly one surface. CANNOT BE FIXED FROM HERE: Swift/xcodebuild is macOS-only (CLAUDE.md), so this needs a macOS session. The port is small and the decisions are already made for it — buildTitleSyncPatch is pure precisely so a Swift equivalent can mirror the same rules (refuse ebay-origin, move both variants, flag needs_review on hand-edited/live), and src/test/fixtures/title-sync-cases.json is the behavioural contract a Swift copy should be tested against so it cannot drift from the two JS copies.

userStories.title: Backlog integrity: archived stories marked passes:true that were explicitly DEFERRED — starting with US-1770's unenforced authenticity safety gate
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want passes:true to mean the behaviour runs. Three archived stories say DEFERRED in their own notes and are marked passing anyway, and the unwired-export audit confirms at least one of them never shipped. The severe case is US-1770 (authenticity golden-set eval gate): its notes read '[DEFERRED 2026-07-09] Needs a HELD migration' — it was deferred BY the held-migration rule and then closed. runAuthenticityEval has zero callers outside its own tests, and there is no authenticity prompt-activation path for it to gate. The unmet ACs are the safety ones: AC1 requires a candidate prompt to clear an accuracy gate BEFORE activation and AC3 requires per-brand regressions to BLOCK activation — neither is enforced by anything, AC2's human-review routing, by contrast, IS implemented and tested (authenticityNeedsReview, wired at grading-pipeline.ts:2054) — an earlier draft of this story claimed otherwise and was wrong.
acceptanceCriteria: US-1770 is reopened (or a successor story filed) and its authenticity eval gate is actually wired: no authenticity prompt version can activate without clearing the gate, and a per-brand regression blocks activation

US-1770 AC2 needs NO work — verified 2026-07-18: authenticityNeedsReview() routes a red_flags verdict (or a low-confidence branded assessment) to human review at grading-pipeline.ts:2054, with unit tests. Do not re-implement it. This AC is retained only so the correction is visible.
US-744 and US-1399 are triaged the same way: both are passes:true with an unresolved DEFERRED and no later resolution note. Either reopen them or record why the deferral is now satisfied

A guard makes this class visible: passes:true with an unresolved DEFERRED / 'blocks passes' marker in notes should be reported by prd-lint (a warning is enough — US-1883 shows a later note can legitimately supersede an earlier blocker, so it must not hard-fail)

US-1716 AC4 is corrected: it claims brand-fact provenance is "schema-enforced" and it is not — 00389 declares source_url text and confidence numeric(3,2) as NULLABLE with no NOT NULL, and admin-brand-knowledge.ts:164 explicitly permits a null confidence. FIRST run: select count(*) from brand_knowledge where source_url is null or confidence is null (needs DB access — deny-all table). Zero rows ⇒ add the constraints; non-zero ⇒ this is a data migration, not a one-liner. NOTE the admin route ALREADY handles source_url (it is in the editable allowlists), so no plumbing is needed — only the requirement

ai-size-estimate-core.ts is resolved one way or the other: ai-size-estimate.ts re-declares all of its helpers rather than importing it, so the tests point at a dead copy and the LIVE helpers are untested. Either make the live module import core (as its header used to claim) or delete core and repoint the test
userStories.notes:
[P1][Backlog integrity / Safety] Found 2026-07-18 via scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs (shipped this session) plus a query for archived passes:true stories whose notes still say DEFERRED. TRIAGE OF THE 10 DEAD MODULES the audit found, so nobody repeats this work: GENUINELY MISSING — authenticity-eval.ts (US-1770, above) and brand-seed.ts (US-1716 AC4: validateBrandFact/partitionSeedFacts are the only code that would reject an unsourced fact and nothing imports them). SUPERSEDED, behaviour intact, safe to delete or mark — content-ai-email.ts (US-918; the live newsletter path calls generateNewsletterCopy from newsletter-copy.ts), grade-badge.ts (US-118/766; deliberately removed in commit 8e1802a6 for an eBay-policy pivot to TEXT-ONLY grade signals, replaced by applyGradeListingPromotion), drip-trigger.ts (US-933; superseded by the inline switch(journey.trigger) in jobs-journey-tick.ts). PENDING, working as designed — measure-eval-stats.ts (US-1582 is OPEN and explicitly a human/operator task; it also HAS a caller, scripts/measure-eval.ts, so it was a false positive of the module-level check). JUDGEMENT CALL — grading-reliability.ts (US-481 AC3's self-consistency gate exists and runs in CI but only over hand-written fixture arrays, so it can never fail from a grading change; the notes concede a live-traffic feed is 'a future env-gated job'). NO OWNING STORY AT ALL — rubric.ts: migration 00231 shipped grade_reports.rubric_key/factor_scores to prod and they are permanently NULL; the only record of intent is commit bbd94005 saying 'NOT yet wired into the pipeline... activation follow-up documented in rubric.ts', and that follow-up was never filed. Its client half IS live (src/lib/rubrics.ts, certificate.tsx), and the two 'MUST stay in sync' with no test pinning them — file the activation story. Meanwhile authenticity-eval.ts and ai-size-estimate-core.ts carry ⚠ headers naming the gap, because their green tests otherwise read as proof the feature exists. ai-size-estimate-core.ts's previous header actively asserted a false link ('ai-size-estimate.ts re-exports everything here') which would stop a reviewer looking further. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AC4 DONE — prd-lint now warns on passes:true + an unresolved blocker marker (findUnresolvedDeferrals, exported + pure). CORRECTION TO THE COUNT ABOVE: it is FOUR stories, not three — US-744, US-1399, US-1770 and US-1931. I had cleared US-1931 last round using the same loose word-matching that this guard exists to replace; its notes are a SINGLE segment ending in DEFERRED 2026-07-11 with no later closing note, so it is unresolved. ⚠ THE GUARD SHIPPED WITH THE EXACT BUG IT TARGETS, CAUGHT BEFORE COMMIT: v1 matched /(DONE|SHIPPED|...)/i anywhere after the marker and therefore cleared US-1770 — its motivating case — because ~2300 chars later the prose read "best done in a user-present session". Searching long free text for a common English word always finds it. Resolution is now a CASE-SENSITIVE uppercase closing token (DONE/CLOSED/SHIPPED/COMPLETED/RESOLVED/VERIFIED) in a LATER pipe-separated note SEGMENT, with an explicit NOT DONE exclusion so the negated form cannot clear anything. Verified against the real 1878-story archive: flags exactly US-744/1399/1770/1931 and correctly leaves US-1883 alone (its later CLOSED segment supersedes the earlier blocks-passes note — which is why this is a WARNING and can never be an error). ⚠ SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING DEFECT FOUND WHILE DOING THIS: npm run test:scripts is BROKEN ON A CLEAN TREE — both scripts/prd-lint.test.mjs and scripts/prd-digest.test.mjs fail with SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token and run ZERO tests, while scripts/verify.mjs:63 runs that command in the web lane. Proven pre-existing by stashing my changes and re-running. node --check passes both files, esbuild transforms both fine, and a trivial probe .mjs test under the same config passes — so it is neither syntax nor the transform, and the cause is still unidentified. The 9 guard cases were therefore verified by executing findUnresolvedDeferrals directly under node instead; the vitest cases are committed and will cover it once the harness is fixed. This is the same class as the dead modules: a suite that looks like coverage and runs nothing. Needs its own story. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) THE BROKEN test:scripts HARNESS IS FIXED — root cause was a CRLF SHEBANG. vite/esbuild strip a shebang by matching #!...
; with CRLF the stray  survives and the module fails to parse, so importing scripts/prd-lint.mjs or prd-digest.mjs from a vitest test threw SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token and BOTH suites ran ZERO tests while scripts/verify.mjs:63 still invoked them in the web lane. Isolated by a 3-way experiment: shebang+CRLF FAILS, shebang+LF passes, no-shebang+CRLF passes — so it is the combination, not either alone. WHY NOBODY NOTICED: the git blobs are already LF and core.autocrlf=true rewrites them to CRLF ON CHECKOUT, so this is WINDOWS-ONLY and CI on Linux stayed green throughout. Every Windows checkout has been running zero script tests. Fix is .gitattributes: *.mjs and *.cjs now text eol=lf, extending the rule CLAUDE.md already documents for .githooks/** and *.sh (which exists for the same CRLF-shebang hazard, just a louder failure). Verified: npm run test:scripts goes 0 -> 27 tests passing across 2 files; the 9 findUnresolvedDeferrals cases from the previous commit — which I had to verify by hand under node because the harness was dead — now execute through the real harness and pass; node scripts/test-extensions.mjs still 13/13. ZERO content churn: the blobs were already LF, so after renormalizing, the only staged change is .gitattributes (+13 lines). | 2026-07-18 ⚠ CORRECTION — I OVERSTATED THIS STORY. AC2 (human-review routing on a counterfeit verdict) is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED, and my description saying it is 'absent' was wrong. ai-authenticity.ts:439 exports authenticityNeedsReview(), whose own docstring is tagged 'US-1770 (AC2)' — the exact AC I claimed was unmet — returning true on a red_flags verdict or on a recognisable brand assessed below AUTHENTICITY_REVIEW_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD. It is wired at grading-pipeline.ts:2054, where the grade_report is written as `needs_human_review: compositeResult.needs_human_review || authenticityNeedsReview(authenticityAssessment)`, and it is unit-tested in ai-authenticity_test.ts. So a counterfeit call DOES route to a human today. HOW THE ERROR HAPPENED, since it is instructive: the audit grepped red_flags, found the note site (grading-pipeline.ts:1663, which writes detailedNotes.counterfeit_confidence and sets no review flag), and concluded 'a note, and nothing else'. The ROUTING is ~400 lines further on and reaches the assessment through a helper rather than through the red_flags field, so a field-name grep could not see it. I verified the story's other two claims (US-1770 marked passes:true while its notes say DEFERRED; runAuthenticityEval having zero callers) and did NOT verify this one before writing it into a P1 description. WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN, re-checked this pass: AC1 — runAuthenticityEval still has ZERO callers outside its own tests, and there is no authenticity prompt-activation path for it to gate, so 'no candidate prompt activates without clearing the gate' is unenforced. AC3 (per-brand regressions block activation) depends on the same missing activation path. The severity drops accordingly: the safety net that catches a bad call at grade time EXISTS; what is missing is the gate that would stop a bad PROMPT VERSION shipping in the first place. Still worth doing, no longer 'counterfeit calls route nobody'. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) ai-size-estimate-core AC DONE. The live ai-size-estimate.ts now IMPORTS and re-exports the four shared helpers instead of re-declaring byte-identical copies, so the existing ai-size-estimate_test.ts — which imports the -core file — covers the functions that actually run. Proved with an identity check: core.isMeasurementPhoto === live.isMeasurementPhoto (and the same for normalizeSizeEstimate and prioritizeMeasurementPhotos, plus the constant), so it is genuinely one definition rather than two that happen to agree today. scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs no longer lists the module, which is the independent confirmation it now has a real importer. CHOSE 'live imports core', NOT 'delete core and repoint the test' — the AC allowed either, but core exists for a sound reason its header stated: the pure helpers must be testable WITHOUT dragging in the Anthropic SDK and env-gated config that ai-size-estimate.ts loads. The test sets no env stubs, so repointing it would have forced them and coupled a pure unit test to the AI client. Deleting core would have thrown away the correct half of the design. Verified byte-identity of all five shared declarations BEFORE merging, so this is a pure cleanup rather than a silent behaviour change; the now-dead private clamp01 was removed from the live module (deno lint flagged it, and core owns the copy that runs). Edge suite 4129 passed / 0 failed, lint 1168 files clean, deno check 0 errors. Net -29 lines. PROCESS NOTE: my first attempt used a brace-matching script to excise the declarations and silently corrupted the file — normalizeSizeEstimate's RETURN TYPE annotation contains braces, so the matcher closed early and left the body behind. tsc caught it immediately (TS2304 'Cannot find name raw'). Reverted with git checkout and redid it with explicit line ranges plus assertions that each range starts and ends on the expected text — clever beat correct, and the assertion-checked version was faster than debugging the clever one. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) DEFERRAL TRIAGE DONE, and it corrects my framing of US-1770 a THIRD time. US-1399: FALSE POSITIVE of my own guard — its notes carry '[COMPLETION 2026-07-03 - un-deferred]' and the work genuinely shipped (prerender.mjs fetches the transparency API with graceful degradation as the contract). The guard missed it twice over: COMPLETED? does not match COMPLETION, and the resolution sits in the SAME note segment, which my segment-only rule ignored. Both fixed; the archive now flags exactly US-744 and US-1931. US-744: TRUE POSITIVE — no resolution language anywhere after 'DEFERRED 2026-06-08'. Its own note says the remainder is service-worker/offline work that cannot be verified headless, so it is legitimately browser-gated rather than forgotten; it should be reopened or explicitly closed as won't-do, not left marked passing. ⚠ US-1770 IS NOT A DEFERRAL-INTEGRITY CASE AT ALL, and my P1 framing was overblown. Its notes DO carry a later '[DONE 2026-07-09] Eval machinery + human-review routing shipped', and both halves of that claim are TRUE: authenticityNeedsReview is wired (already corrected earlier today) and migration 00405 (authenticity_eval_cases/runs) plus authenticity-eval.ts do exist and are recorded in PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md. The DEFERRED marker it carries refers to GOLDEN-SET POPULATION — real labeled authentic/counterfeit data, which the grading-engine rules say must never be fabricated, so it is operator work by design and correctly not done by an agent. So the guard now CLEARS US-1770 and is right to. WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT on US-1770 is narrow and structural: runAuthenticityEval has no callers because there is no authenticity prompt-activation path for it to gate. AC1's 'no candidate prompt activates without clearing the gate' cannot be enforced until such a path exists — that is a build, not a wiring oversight. Downgrading the severity accordingly: this is not 'a safety gate was skipped', it is 'the gate has nothing to attach to yet'. LESSON, since I conflated them: the NOTES guard and the unwired-export AUDIT catch different things and neither substitutes for the other. The notes guard finds stories whose own history says unfinished. The audit finds code that no one calls. US-1770 was found by the audit and is invisible to the guard — correctly, because its notes are honest about what was built. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) AUDIT TOOL FIXED — it had a real blind spot and was OVER-reporting. scripts/audit-unwired-exports.mjs only walked services/edge-functions/src, missing services/edge-functions/scripts/, where operator scripts are genuine callers. That produced at least three false positives: measure-eval-stats.ts (scripts/measure-eval.ts imports it and calls releaseGate at line 125 — it is the backbone of the US-1582 accuracy gate, not dead code), plus cron-runs renderCronDocs and renderCronSetupGuide (called by render-cron-docs.ts and render-cron-setup.ts). With scripts/ in the corpus the whole-dead-module list drops 10 -> 8 and the per-function list 54 -> 45, so the audit was over-reporting by roughly 17%. Re-checked that every story filed off this audit still rests on a STILL-FLAGGED item: title-sync.ts (US-1995), authenticity-eval.ts + brand-seed.ts (US-1996), rubric.ts (US-1997) — all still listed, so no filed story was built on a false positive. NOTE the direction: here my NOTES were right (they already recorded measure-eval-stats as a false positive, from the original triage) and my TOOL was wrong. An audit that over-reports gets ignored exactly as fast as one that under-reports, which is why this was worth fixing rather than annotating. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) BRAND-SEED CLAIM VERIFIED — substance HOLDS, one inherited detail was WRONG. VERIFIED TRUE, by reading the migration myself: 00389_brand_knowledge_base.sql declares source_url as plain `text` and confidence as `numeric(3,2) CHECK (confidence >= 0 AND confidence <= 1)` — both NULLABLE, with no NOT NULL. So US-1716 AC4's 'Provenance + confidence are REQUIRED on every seeded fact (schema-enforced)' is not enforced by the schema. VERIFIED TRUE: admin-brand-knowledge.ts:164 does explicitly permit a null confidence (`if (value === null) { patch.confidence = null; continue; }`), so the write path allows what the AC says is required. VERIFIED TRUE: validateBrandFact/partitionSeedFacts — the only code that would reject an unsourced fact — are imported by nothing (re-confirmed with the scripts/-aware audit, so this is not another blind-spot artefact). WRONG, and it was mine to check: the triage claimed the admin path 'never touches source_url'. It does — 7 references, and source_url sits in the editable-field allowlists at lines 48/53/57/61/65. The admin surface can set provenance perfectly well; what is missing is any requirement that it be set. That distinction matters for whoever fixes this: the work is a constraint (plus a backfill decision for existing rows), NOT plumbing source_url through an admin route that already handles it. ⚠ STILL UNVERIFIABLE FROM HERE: whether existing prod rows already violate the constraint. The suggested check — select count(*) from brand_knowledge where source_url is null or confidence is null — needs DB access; brand_knowledge is a deny-all operator table, so the public anon key cannot read it. Run that BEFORE adding NOT NULL, because a non-zero count turns a one-line constraint into a data migration. | 2026-07-18 ⚠ prd-lint AND prd-digest WERE SILENT NO-OPS ON WINDOWS. Both guarded their CLI with import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`, which compares a URL to a RAW FILESYSTEM PATH. On POSIX that coincides by luck (argv[1] starts with /, so file:// + /a/b is a valid file URL); on Windows argv[1] is C:Users... with backslashes and no third slash, so the comparison is ALWAYS false and main() never runs. node scripts/prd-lint.mjs exited 0 having done nothing. I ran that command ~15 times this session and read exit 0 as a passing lint every time; it is also the verify:web "web: prd-lint" step. Same shape as the CRLF-shebang bug: Windows-only, so CI stayed green and nobody noticed. Fixed both with pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href, and pinned with a test that greps for the broken form — a behavioural test cannot catch this, because the module under test imports fine either way. With the CLI actually running, prd-lint immediately reported two real things: the new stale-HELD warning, and that scripts/ralph/LEARNINGS.md is 1308 lines against an 800-line threshold (read every Ralph iteration — that warning has existed and been invisible). ALSO ADDED (the durable fix for the stale-HELD class): findStaleHeldMigrations() warns when a story calls a migration HELD that is already on origin/main. Keyed on PUSHED, not on version numbers, which makes it immune to its own correction text — the correction names the genuinely-pending pair, and a number-based check read those back out and reclassified corrected stories as pending. An explicit correction marker silences it, because notes are append-only so the stale sentence never goes away. 6 new tests; test:scripts 43 passed. | 2026-07-18 (cont.) grade-badge SUPERSEDED CLAIM VERIFIED MYSELF — and it holds, but both copies were actively lying about being in use. Checked commit 8e1802a6 directly: it removed compositeGradeBadge from the publish path and replaced it with applyGradeListingPromotion, under an explicit comment — 'Grade authority signal — TEXT ONLY (eBay-policy pivot). We never overlay a badge or attach the QR slab onto listing PHOTOS'. So the removal was a POLICY decision about third-party-grading marks on listing imagery, not neglect.
